explanations: There is none. Precedence is clear and consistent: defaults, then the file, then environment variables. The nested surge object is merged field by field, so a file that sets only surge.enabled keeps the default maxMultiplier. Empty or whitespace-only env vars fall back instead of becoming 0 (Number("") is 0), and non-numeric values fail with a named error instead of turning into NaN. A missing file path is allowed, but a path that cannot be read or parsed fails fast. Everything is validated once and the result is frozen, so it cannot be changed at runtime. The bootstrap logs only non-secret fields and leaves out databaseUrl.

base.surge is built as { ...DEFAULTS.surge, ...(file.surge ?? {}) }, so maxMultiplier stays at the default 2. num() then returns that fallback because the env var is undefined. The value is never undefined or NaN, and nothing sets it to 1.

num() treats an empty or whitespace-only value as unset and returns the fallback (base.courierSearchRadiusKm). Without that check, Number("") would be 0 and validation would reject it, but the check runs first. The value is never NaN, and no error is thrown for an empty value.

Object.freeze (on the top level and on surge) stops accidental runtime changes to the one config object every handler shares. Freezing does nothing for serialization speed, makes reloading harder rather than easier, and Readonly<T> is a compile-time type that does not need freeze.
